title: Unified Optimize Playbook — recommendation cards, diff-preview, and safe revert flow
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and deliver a single, operator-friendly Optimize 'playbook' experience in the Redwood Console that synthesizes batching/caching recommendations into actionable cards, provides a clear side-by-side diff preview with cost/latency estimates, and offers a staged, auditable apply + safe revert flow. The goal is to make automated cost-reduction suggestions trustworthy and reversible for production workloads without operator surprise.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards surface batching and cache suggestions with clear confidence and expected cost delta
Diff preview shows before/after runtime config, token-level cost estimate, and estimated 95th-percentile latency impact
Operators can run a dry-run preview that simulates expected savings and highlights potential regressions
Apply flow supports staged rollout targets (canary, cohort, global) with configurable monitoring windows
Every apply creates an immutable audit entry containing operator, timestamp, config snapshot, and links to the diff preview
Rollback workflow supports both soft revert (gradual rollback via rollout policy) and hard rollback (immediate revert to snapshot) with single-click actions
UI has contextual safety gating when suggestions increase latency or change kernel/quantization settings
Backend APIs /optimize/preview and /optimize/apply have schema validation and return a stable preview-id for audit linkage
tasks: Finalize PRD and example playbook scenarios (batching-heavy vs cache-heavy workloads)
Design recommendation card visual treatment and compact vs expanded states (Figma mock)
Spec side-by-side diff UI with token cost meter and latency band visualization
Implement preview backend: simulate cost/latency and produce preview-id (ENG)
Wire apply flow with staged rollout controller and hooks to console alerts (ENG)
Create audit model: immutable apply records + config snapshots (ENG)
Add rollback UI flows and automated telemetry to validate revert success
Run internal dogfood on three Redwood tenants and iterate on wording
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff with ENG, DES, and SRE. Agreed scope: cards + preview + staged apply. Decided to defer in-console cost simulation of KV cache hit-rate to Phase 2.
2025-02-20: DES shipped first Figma screens for compact cards and expanded diff modal. Engineering notes: diff must include runtime-1.20 kernel mapping metadata.
2025-02-25: ENG prototype for /optimize/preview returns stable preview-id and delta estimates; simulation uses historical traffic traces for cost projection.
2025-02-28: PM review with Legal and Compliance — audit entries must persist beyond retention TTL for enterprise customers; added release flag for extended retention.
2025-03-01: UX review: safety gating copy reworded to emphasize 'expected' not 'guaranteed' savings; added tooltip linking to eval tests and CI checks.
review_feedback: DES: prefer card CTA 'Open preview' rather than 'Apply' to reduce accidental changes
ENG: require preview-id propagation to telemetry and logs to simplify incident triage
SRE: add automated canary abort condition when error-rate or p95 latency increases > 20%
Security: ensure apply endpoint requires operator MFA for customers with strict RBAC
notes: Trade-offs: we will not auto-apply quantization changes without explicit operator confirmation due to possible quality regressions.
Edge case: recommendations that change model variant require explicit 'model-compatibility' check; ENG to surface failing tests in preview response.
Metric hooks: link preview-id to existing runtime tracing so operators can correlate apply -> metric regressions quickly.
Open question: retention window for audit snapshots for Self-Host customers (needs legal guidance)
